goal: Locate a tuned non-meta baseline
comparison: AdamW cosine across seven peak learning rates
why: Establish the denominator before claiming improvements
result: Cosine peaks near 3e-3; earlier 1e-3 peak was wrong.
reason: The earlier reference understated the scheduled baseline.
scope: R18/C10 augmented, 100 epochs; SW and fxcos differ in warmup.
original_question: Is there a tuned non-meta baseline at all, and where does its learning rate peak?

goal: Test whether scheduling explains the baseline gap
comparison: Fixed AdamW, MetaOptimize, AdamW cosine, SGDm cosine
why: Separate adaptation from scheduled learning-rate gains
result: Meta beats fixed AdamW by 1.551 pp; scheduled SGD wins by 1.807 pp.
reason: The scheduled denominator changes the method comparison.
scope: 100 epochs; each selected peak; augmentation on; meta guard occupancy unavailable.
original_question: Is the method-vs-baseline gap caused by the cosine SCHEDULE?

goal: Validate the experimental harness
comparison: SGD momentum cosine against a registered accuracy band
why: Exclude a generally broken training harness
result: SGD reaches the expected band; the best primary cell is 95.124%.
reason: A known reference recipe reproduces expected accuracy.
scope: R18/C10, 100 epochs, n=5 per learning rate.
original_question: Does the experimental harness reproduce a known-good reference, i.e. is the deficit a property of the method rather than of our code?

goal: Close the baseline deficit with longer training
comparison: Matched recipe families at 100, 300, 600 epochs
why: Test the short-horizon explanation
result: A roughly two-point deficit persists at 300 and 600 epochs.
reason: More training did not close this configured baseline deficit.
scope: 100-epoch historical series was initially mismatched; 300/600 matched AdamW recipes.
original_question: Does the deficit close if MetaOptimize is given a longer horizon (the parent paper's implicit defence)?

goal: Replicate baseline superiority across architecture sizes
comparison: Cosine and best available meta arms on R34/R50
why: Check whether the deficit is R18-specific
result: Cosine remains stronger on R34 and R50; R34 pooling is selection-inflated.
reason: The baseline advantage survives the tested architecture changes.
scope: C10, 100 epochs; baseline only two learning rates on each target.
original_question: Does the baseline's win survive a change of architecture (is it an R18 accident)?

goal: Audit comparison fairness
comparison: Budget, tuning allocation, augmentation, and paper configuration
why: Find unresolved denominator mismatches
result: Unaugmented CIFAR-10 is measured; method tuning and unaugmented CIFAR-100 remain limited.
reason: Two method alpha0 cells do not bracket its unaugmented optimum.
scope: CAU1 completed; historical NOT SUBMITTED text is stale. No new training implied.
original_question: Was the method-vs-baseline comparison FAIR (matched budget, matched search budget, the paper's own setup)?

goal: Test the unaugmented baseline deficit
comparison: Seven SGD rates versus two MetaOptimize initializations
why: Address the parent-paper augmentation objection
result: Unaugmented SGD beats the better registered meta cell by 3.617 pp.
reason: The registered CIFAR-10 deficit survives without augmentation.
scope: CAU1, n=3 fresh seeds per arm, one batch, 100 epochs; ingest uncommitted.
original_question: Does the denominator survive in the parent paper's OWN, UNAUGMENTED setting -- does a TUNED non-meta baseline still beat MetaOptimize when `AUGMENT=0` on every arm (the last fairness objection with teeth, 202)?

goal: Measure a partitioning benefit
comparison: Scalar and partitioned arms with shared versus tuned steps
why: Separate partition choice from meta-step tuning
result: Tuning greatly shrinks the scalar-layerwise gap; a small residual remains.
reason: A scoped partition benefit survives tuning controls.
scope: R18/C10 SGDm/Lion, a0=1e-3; multi-batch census versus later within-batch controls.
original_question: Does a finer partition of the step size help at all?

goal: Test tolerance to excessive meta steps
comparison: Each partition’s loss above its selected meta-step peak
why: Measure robustness beyond peak accuracy
result: Scalar loses more under excessive meta steps; the old nodewise slope is stale.
reason: The ordering survives the registered primary-metric reanalysis.
scope: Canonical C10 surface; some slopes depend on n=1 cells; clamp caveats remain.
original_question: Is the granularity axis just a reparameterisation of the meta-stepsize axis?

goal: Resolve accuracy differences among tuned partitions
comparison: Layerwise, six-block, nodewise and weightwise at selected meta steps
why: Avoid ranking noise and mixed batch compositions
result: Small coarse-partition differences remain vulnerable to batch composition; weightwise is lower.
reason: The old 0.254-point ranking lacked a balanced batch comparison.
scope: C10; original nodewise peak n=1 was later expanded; no blanket partition tie.
original_question: Is the difference AMONG partitions (as opposed to partition-vs-none) resolvable?

goal: Recover weightwise accuracy by tuning
comparison: wm9 weightwise meta-step ladder versus registered 92.2–92.9 band
why: Test whether mistuning explained the finest-partition deficit
result: wm9 peaks at 91.015%; every run misses the registered recovery band.
reason: The measured interior plateau stays below the recovery band.
scope: 10 completed runs, n=2 at five steps; tw0 later closes 100-epoch guard caveat.
original_question: Does per-weight granularity fail STRUCTURALLY, or does it recover under tuning?

goal: Establish a base-optimizer interaction
comparison: Granularity under SGDm, AdamW, and Lion at two initializations
why: Test the proposed coordinate-normalization explanation
result: Interaction depends on initialization; bo7 completed but does not establish a universal mechanism.
reason: AdamW reverses at proper initialization; Lion also contradicts the mechanism.
scope: 100-epoch accuracy census and separate 20-epoch bo7 field measurement; never conflate.
original_question: H4 — does granularity help under SGDm and do nothing under AdamW (the base-optimizer interaction)?

goal: Explain catastrophic weightwise collapse
comparison: Lion versus Adam meta updates and beta guard
why: Separate runaway dynamics from residual partition weakness
result: Guarding removes catastrophic collapse; a sizable weightwise accuracy deficit remains.
reason: The guard fixes collapse but not the measured accuracy loss.
scope: R18/C10 a0=1e-6 ms=1e-3; not a universal claim across all tuning.
original_question: Why does per-weight granularity collapse to 10% accuracy — numerics or the method?

goal: Flatten the fully tuned granularity ladder
comparison: Best observed meta step for all five partition scales
why: Include the previously missing weightwise rung
result: Completed wm9/tw0 refute a flat ladder; the weightwise rung stays lower.
reason: The finest partition fails to recover through the tested tuning.
scope: The MASTER OPEN token predates wm9 and tw0; coarse rankings retain batch caveats.
original_question: **Is the granularity ladder flat once EVERY rung sits at its own optimal ms?**

goal: Validate shared-step attribution to partition choice
comparison: Nodewise minus layerwise at common versus individually tuned steps
why: Expose a tuning-induced change of sign
result: The contrast changes from +1.138 to −0.360 pp after tuning.
reason: A single shared meta step confounds the attribution.
scope: Shared control crosses batches, n=2 versus 2; use Welch, not paired inference.
original_question: Does a granularity contrast at a SHARED meta-stepsize measure the partition?

goal: Establish an optimal-granularity reversal over time
comparison: Layerwise versus nodewise through epochs 10–40
why: Connect partition preference to training horizon
result: The reversal holds at shared ms=1e-3; tuning reverses the trajectory.
reason: The observation is real but the optimum interpretation does not survive.
scope: br6+bl5, seven within-batch differences, two ceilings; no independent budget randomization.
original_question: Does the accuracy-OPTIMAL granularity reverse as the training horizon grows?

goal: Generalize reversal shape and crossing time
comparison: Forty-one observed configuration cells across models and datasets
why: Check whether the crossing is universal
result: Rising differences occur in 24/29 eligible cells; crossing time does not generalize.
reason: The direction is common within a stratum; timing varies.
scope: 27/41 all cells versus 24/29 adapting eligible cells; these are not new jobs.
original_question: Is the U-in-training-time shape general, and is the CROSSING EPOCH general?

goal: Preserve the reversal after meta-step tuning
comparison: Layerwise at 1e-4 versus nodewise at 3e-4
why: Test the main reversal’s tuning explanation
result: Nodewise starts ahead and declines to −0.360 pp; original reversal fails.
reason: Registered T-B confirms the counterprediction, not the original headline.
scope: hz9 plus licensed rs controls; n=5 versus 5 unpaired; ±0.50 endpoint materiality bar.
original_question: Does the reversal survive letting EACH ARM sit at its own optimal meta-stepsize?

goal: Measure fixed-step fragility
comparison: Constant AdamW across seven learning-rate cells
why: Provide a meaningful robustness denominator
result: Small fixed rates undertrain; lr=0.1 collapses in all three runs.
reason: Fixed-step performance is strongly sensitive to the chosen rate.
scope: Seven points spanning five decades; small rate trains weakly, not literally zero learning.
original_question: Does a genuinely FIXED learning rate collapse at small initial step sizes (does the robustness claim have a denominator)?

goal: Test robustness across initial learning rates
comparison: MetaOptimize across the same seven initializations
why: Evaluate the paper’s low-initialization robustness claim
result: Low-alpha0 accuracy stays near 91.6%; the highest-rate cell is not robust.
reason: The low-end advantage holds; whole-grid flatness does not.
scope: R18/C10 AdamW/Adam six-block, augmented, n=3 per cell; guard caveat.
original_question: Is MetaOptimize flat over several decades of alpha0 (the parent paper's own claim, never tested here before)?

goal: Improve robustness over scheduled training
comparison: Equal-weight grid means for meta and cosine
why: Avoid unstable threshold-width comparisons
result: Primary grid-mean advantage is 3.159 pp; six-cell sensitivity gives 4.680 pp.
reason: The advantage survives both stated grid reductions.
scope: Chosen grid conditional; cosine account/batch composition differs; legacy +5.094/+4.941 uses last20.
original_question: Against a TUNED SCHEDULE (not a constant LR), is MetaOptimize still more robust?

goal: Test robustness at a longer budget
comparison: 100 versus 300 epochs at four grid extremes
why: Check whether startup delay creates the robustness shape
result: The registered band comparison was stable on the matched extreme cells.
reason: The selected long-budget follow-up did not reverse the registered reading.
scope: Only constant and meta arms, four alpha0 extremes, n=2 at 300; not full three-arm grid.
original_question: Is that robustness shape an artefact of a 100-epoch budget (arm B pays a startup tax at small alpha0)?

goal: Audit threshold-based robustness claims
comparison: Three reductions of the same robustness runs
why: Detect verdict sensitivity to arbitrary thresholds
result: Three threshold-width verdicts reversed and were withdrawn.
reason: Shared-grid truncation and tiny threshold crossings changed the apparent width.
scope: No new training; retain grid-mean result with explicit chosen-grid sensitivity.
original_question: Earlier width-based readings of Idea 3 ('MetaOptimize is/is not flatter on threshold X')

goal: Transfer the granularity gain across model sizes
comparison: Scalar and layerwise on R10/R18/R34/R50
why: Locate architecture dependence of the original premise
result: The gap shrinks with scale and reverses for R50 at small alpha0.
reason: The gain is strongly model-dependent at the shared meta step.
scope: sc matched first-three-seed comparison; R50 sc50 n=2; all C10 and shared ms.
original_question: Does the granularity gain survive model scale?

goal: Reproduce the ResNet-50 layerwise deficit
comparison: R50 scalar versus layerwise at two initializations
why: Find a setting where layerwise loses
result: R50 layerwise loses 1.356 pp at 1e-6 but gains 1.130 at 1e-3.
reason: Layerwise loses only at the smaller tested initialization.
scope: sc50 n=2 per arm; later a2g3 completed and remained SPLIT/UNRESOLVED.
original_question: Is there ANY architecture where the parent paper's premise (layerwise loses to scalar) reproduces on CIFAR-10?

goal: Transfer granularity gains to CIFAR-100
comparison: Scalar, six-block, layerwise at two initializations
why: Test dataset dependence of partition ordering
result: Large fixed-step gaps replicate; six-block/layerwise ordering changes relative to CIFAR-10.
reason: The gap transfers while the partition ordering is dataset-dependent.
scope: c100+c100b n=5 each; shared ms=1e-3, not individually tuned target optima.
original_question: Does granularity transfer to a second dataset (CIFAR-100), and does the ORDERING transfer?

goal: Audit the claimed cost of finer partitions
comparison: Correct six-block, layerwise, nodewise, weightwise labels
why: Check a consequential ordering error
result: Six-block was mislabeled finer; nodewise beats layerwise and weightwise loses.
reason: The claimed 17.2-point cost compared a coarser partition.
scope: C100 a0=1e-3; c100f node/weight n=3; layerwise controls cross batches.
original_question: 'Finer than layerwise costs 17.2 pp on CIFAR-100'

goal: Separate startup delay from partition performance
comparison: Initialization ladders at 20 and 100 epochs
why: Check whether short runs exaggerate granularity effects
result: Startup effects are large; 100-epoch differences remain at the tested shared step.
reason: The 20-epoch design also changes pooling and has one seed.
scope: p2/p3 n=1; a0L 100-epoch n=2; explicitly separate shrink and plain arms.
original_question: Is the granularity result an alpha0=1e-6 startup artefact?

goal: Erase the granularity gap with training time
comparison: Windows at epochs 100, 205, 300 on identical trajectories
why: Test a pure acceleration explanation
result: Granularity remains near 3.4 pp; shrink benefits attenuate strongly.
reason: The longer shared-step trajectory does not erase the partition gap.
scope: e300 n=2; windows from the same 300-epoch runs, not independent budgets.
original_question: Is granularity a SPEED effect that a longer budget erases (the reading of the parent paper's ImageNet null)?

goal: Verify pooling inversion and scalar crossover
comparison: Reaudit horizon tables using matched primary windows
why: Check a previously promoted headline
result: Neither inversion nor scalar crossover survives the corrected stratification and metric.
reason: Best-test selection, mixed initialization, and mislabeled operators created the headline.
scope: No zpool 300-epoch runs; additive and shrink must keep their actual operator labels.
original_question: 'Pooling gains INVERT between 100 and 300 epochs, and scalar overtakes plain layerwise' — once called the strongest result in the project

goal: Beat the tuned baseline with a cosine prior
comparison: Idea-1 meta arms and their available controls
why: Combine adaptation with explicit annealing
result: Idea 1 missed its stopping-rule baseline; its exact schedule remains unidentified.
reason: Accuracy did not clear the registered baseline requirement.
scope: I1, n=3 per main arm, 100 epochs; no saved schedule specification.
original_question: IDEA 1 — put a cosine prior on the learned step size: alpha_t = cosine(t) * exp(beta_t)

goal: Choose partitions using tensor correlation
comparison: Measured adjacent versus random tensor sign agreement
why: Find a predictive partition-selection signal
result: The powered tensor-level correlation contrast was null; the direction was abandoned.
reason: The signal needed by the proposed partition rule was absent.
scope: kt2 existing 100-epoch weightwise runs; coordinate-level null underpowered; zero additional training.
original_question: IDEA 2 — choose the partition from MEASURED meta-gradient correlation between tensors

goal: Find a tunable shrinkage strength
comparison: Per-step M0 shrink across a lambda ladder
why: Implement partial hierarchical pooling
result: The operator saturates; the alleged tunable pooling interpretation was withdrawn.
reason: Per-step application turns most tested lambdas into near-full shrinkage.
scope: Primary ladder available separately; historical best_test improvements are not primary evidence.
original_question: M0 SHRINK — pull each group's beta toward the group mean every step, with a tunable coefficient lambda

goal: Close the weightwise deficit with pooling
comparison: Shrink, additive, and zpool weightwise controls
why: Rescue the finest partition using shared information
result: zpool rescues weightwise accuracy but still misses the stronger coarse partitions.
reason: A rescue exists, but it does not close the competitive deficit.
scope: R18/C10 a0=1e-6; operator-specific directions differ and must remain separated.
original_question: Does pooling CLOSE the per-weight deficit?

goal: Find an interior additive optimum
comparison: Layerwise additive r curve against both endpoints
why: Test whether partial sharing improves accuracy
result: A local interior optimum exists; g4m preserves +0.821 pp after meta-step optimization.
reason: The later joint sweep defeats the pure meta-step explanation.
scope: Small-alpha0 R18/C10 setting; additive benefit is not proof of original two-level proposal.
original_question: M1 ADDITIVE — is there an INTERIOR pooling optimum (partial pooling beating both endpoints)?

goal: Validate the additive pooling interpretation
comparison: Additive and true-pooling endpoint controls across granularities
why: Test whether r is the claimed sharing mechanism
result: Additive endpoints are not true pooling; the “merely meta-step” explanation was later refuted.
reason: g4m overturns one explanation without validating the original operator interpretation.
scope: Separate algebraic endpoint failure from empirically rejected pure-ms explanation.
original_question: Is M1's r actually a POOLING dial (the mechanism the whole hierarchical story rests on)?

goal: Improve accuracy through true full pooling
comparison: zpool r=0 versus plain layerwise
why: Test the claimed full-pooling benefit directly
result: True full pooling reduces accuracy by about three points.
reason: The earlier positive endpoint was an additive arm, not true pooling.
scope: Use within-zsw endpoint contrast or explicit pooled controls, never mix their effect estimates.
original_question: Does FULL pooling help (+1.39 pp), as carried in the handoff doc?

goal: Establish a competitive tuned pooling method
comparison: Additive and plain controls with meta-step tuning
why: Check whether another hyperparameter buys accuracy
result: Older partial tuning favored plain; g4m later preserves a local additive advantage.
reason: The original broad domination claim did not test the joint sweep.
scope: No conclusion of universal pooling dominance; neither local result clears tuned non-meta baseline.
original_question: Even taking the curve at face value, is pooling worth doing?

goal: Preserve the additive optimum at proper initialization
comparison: Additive r curves at alpha0=1e-6 and 1e-3
why: Test dependence on slow initial learning
result: Most interior gain disappears; the whole curve does not become flat.
reason: The remaining local improvement misses the stated materiality threshold.
scope: ac plus exactly matched earlier controls; multiple batch families; r=1 still substantially lower.
original_question: Does the M1 interior optimum survive a non-crippled initialisation?

goal: Transfer the additive optimum
comparison: r curves across architecture, dataset, and initialization
why: Test whether the local optimum supports a general method
result: R10/R34 small-alpha0 optima exist; C100 fails; R50 follow-up remains unresolved.
reason: Transfer is conditional; the old “nowhere” claim is false.
scope: R34 a0=1e-3 still lacks a full curve; a2g3 36 runs completed.
original_question: Does the M1 optimum transfer to another architecture or dataset?

goal: Improve good partitions with meta-gradient pooling
comparison: zpool r sweeps for layerwise and weightwise
why: Test a true-pooling alternative to additive updates
result: Weightwise is rescued; layerwise shows no material interior improvement.
reason: The benefit is a fine-partition rescue, with interior step-size confounding.
scope: zpool 100-epoch ladder; zmpool only four 20-epoch endpoint checks, not a full sweep.
original_question: Does pooling in META-GRADIENT space (the confound-free operator) have an interior optimum?

goal: Identify a scaling law for optimal r
comparison: R10/R18/R34 argmaxes versus parameter count
why: Predict the sharing setting from model size
result: Argmaxes decrease with size, but batch noise and grid resolution prevent a scaling law.
reason: Cross-family peak margins are below the measured batch floor.
scope: Small alpha0 only; proper initialization breaks the trend; no further compute was recommended.
original_question: Is there a scale law for the pooling optimum (r* ~ 1/N)?

goal: Check the claimed excess sign agreement
comparison: Layerwise and weightwise agreement vs their own independence nulls
why: Avoid mixing group counts and null expectations.
result: 53.1% belongs to 62 groups; its independence expectation is 55.07%.
reason: The published sentence combined the wrong arm and wrong null.
scope: R18/C10 sign probes. Weightwise agreement is 50.005–50.028%, not 53.1%; null depends on coordinate count. Later correlation measurements use a different, calibrated variance instrument; this correction does not imply independence.
original_question: Do per-weight meta-gradients agree in sign far more than independence allows? ('53.1% of 11.17M against a null of 50.0000 +-0.0015%')

goal: Test inverse-square-root noise averaging
comparison: Measured drift slopes vs the square-root averaging prediction
why: Check the campaign's noise-averaging premise.
result: Directional evidence conflicts with square-root averaging; censored slope magnitudes remain unquotable.
reason: The measured scaling does not match the registered expectation.
scope: Keep drift versus group count and drift versus group size separate. Some numerical slopes include Lion-censored points; do not plot them as clean estimates. The one contrary two-point R10 startup subspan is retained. This is a test of the campaign's premise, not a refutation of Adam-mini, Adalayer, or SGG.
original_question: Does meta-gradient noise average down like 1/sqrt(N) as the partition gets finer (the premise coarse partitions are sold on)?

goal: Detect correlation after step sizes adapt
comparison: Frozen vs free beta at the same R18 configuration
why: Test whether dependence survives adaptation.
result: Adapted correlation remains measurable: 8.458e-8, independently replicated at 8.888e-8.
reason: The adapted estimate exceeds its own resolution floor.
scope: R18/C10, alpha0=1e-3, steady half of 20 epochs. CORRECTIONS34 matched pair: fz-w-a3 n=5 versus p7-r18-w n=10; rho_s 1.925e-6 versus 8.458e-8. CORRECTIONS47's 8.888e-8 is a separate fr5 replication and must not inherit n=10. Pooled-floor estimates are lower bounds. Published channel percentages do not sum to 100%; do not make a normalized stacked chart from them.
original_question: Are per-weight meta-gradients correlated AT THE ADAPTED OPERATING POINT (not just off-equilibrium)?

goal: Measure effective independence across model and dataset families
comparison: Free vs frozen beta across four architecture/dataset combinations
why: Quantify dependence at the adapted operating point.
result: Under SGDm, per-weight effective independence retains 16–55% over epochs 10–20.
reason: The fraction remains below independence across all four tested families.
scope: Variance-derived N_eff/m = 1/[1+(m-1)rho_s], dimensionless effective-independence fraction, not signal percentage. SGDm base, 20-epoch runs, steady half; free 0.163/0.481/0.552/0.305 for R10/R18/R34/C100. Later AdamW, longer-window and cc1 tests defeat universal or predictive interpretations.
original_question: How much of the independent information their count implies do per-weight meta-gradients actually carry? (N_eff/m)

goal: Preserve effective independence in later training windows
comparison: Epochs 10–20 vs 20–40 at each granularity
why: Check whether early measurements describe later training.
result: Nodewise and weightwise decline; layerwise change remains unresolved.
reason: The effective-independence fraction changes substantially in the finer partitions.
scope: R18/C10; br6 n=4 per rung, all 12 seeds box-free. Changes are -0.0359/-0.1260/-0.3556 for layer/node/weight. Layerwise is a resolution-limited bound, not evidence of stationarity. No budget-coupled schedule exists: this is a window/time contrast, not an independent causal budget intervention.
original_question: Is N_eff/m stationary in training time, or is the headline a 20-epoch sentence?

goal: Keep effective-independence measurements robust to guard changes
comparison: Published guard boxes vs measured box-free configurations
why: Test whether clipping creates the measurement headline.
result: Box removal changes N_eff/m only −0.006 to +0.024 across four families.
reason: All shifts stay within the registered measurement tolerance.
scope: 20 epochs; tested configurations only. Box-free family fractions: R10 .1571, R18 .5045, R34 .5474, C100 .3124. R18 four-box span .076 against historical .10 tolerance. Do not generalize the row's '+.027 pp accuracy-neutral' aside: fa1 and later audits show accuracy effects depend on recipe, bound and horizon.
original_question: Is N_eff/m an artefact of the BETA_CLIP guard box every run sits inside?

goal: Test gradual adaptation of the correlation profile
comparison: Frozen beta vs two valid meta-step settings
why: Distinguish a gradual response from a switch.
result: N_eff/m rises 0.042 → 0.129 → 0.481 as meta-step increases.
reason: The intermediate setting lands between the two endpoint profiles.
scope: R18/C10, ml5, 20 epochs, n=3 per rung. Profile exponent .343→.219→.081 and k=1 suppression 1→3.37→21.09. The ms=1e-2 rung is guard-dominated and excluded from this conclusion. 'High-pass' describes scale-selective measured suppression, not an established causal theory of optimization.
original_question: Is a step-size adapter a HIGH-PASS FILTER on meta-gradient correlation — and is it a dial or a switch?

goal: Verify short-range correlation beyond estimator artifacts
comparison: Corrected scale profiles vs exchangeable and independence models
why: Remove heterogeneity before interpreting the profile.
result: Frozen-beta profiles fall 16.6–264.6× across the four tested families.
reason: The falling profiles survive the corrected independence floor.
scope: Off-equilibrium/frozen beta, 20 epochs, n=2 per arm. rho_w is an implied sign-correlation parameter, not marginal-sign E(u). Steady R18 corrected span69.3 versus uncorrected165.5. Free-beta profiles flatten; R10 free exchangeability is undecided at7.8× rather than universally accepted. Do not call the shape dataset- or architecture-independent beyond these four combinations.
original_question: Off the meta-optimum, does the correlation have a RANGE (short-range, channel-scaled) or is the falling profile an estimator artefact?

goal: Test whether row means represent within-row structure
comparison: Observed row structure vs size-preserving within-tensor regrouping nulls
why: Test the quantity a rowwise meta-step aggregates.
result: Most marginal-sign variation remains within rows; clean row means explain very little.
reason: The measured structure is poorly represented by the row means.
scope: 58 weightwise plus67 nodewise arms, multiple regimes. The measured object is meta-gradient z, not the training gradient G from Adam-mini. Distinguish total across-tensor variation from within-tensor row variation; R_tensor_cor86.88–97.06% does not say rows are individually identifiable.
original_question: Adam-mini's ACTUAL premise: does the row mean represent its row (so a per-row step size is a good approximation)?

goal: Find reproducible architecture-linked row structure
comparison: Anomalous vs clean runs, then row identity across seeds
why: Separate real within-run structure from stable row identity.
result: Anomalous runs have real structure, but the responsible row identities do not reproduce.
reason: Within-run structure is strong; cross-seed identity stays near its null.
scope: Conv-only R_row_cor7.216–49.412% in10 exceptional arms versus0–.448% clean; no dead-coordinate saturation in58 arms. Alternative hypotheses H_A and H_C fail. Coordinate time-series mechanism remains unmeasured; tensor-mean reconstruction was null and does not substitute for it.
original_question: Do 10 anomalous arms carry genuine conv-row structure, and is it architectural or dynamical?

goal: Detect a coherent convolution-filter interaction
comparison: Output–input channel interaction vs a within-tensor permutation null
why: Distinguish a filter object from additive channel effects.
result: All 50 clean arms miss the 1.10 interaction threshold.
reason: Measured interaction ratios span only 0.811–1.041.
scope: F_int is a sum-of-squares ratio, dimensionless. Small-scale marginal structure remains, but a coherent3×3 filter interaction is not detected. The original blanket 'no filter object exists' should be written as a scoped failure of this registered interaction test. DONE; no rerun requested.
original_question: Is the 3x3 convolution FILTER a coherent structural object in the meta-gradient field?

goal: Locate a stable scale of marginal sign structure
comparison: Field block-size curves across trajectory and meta-step settings
why: Check whether the measured scale survives changed dynamics.
result: Peaks cluster within one rung; four clean arms remain bounded by the ladder edge.
reason: Location is stable at tested resolution, but not fully bracketed.
scope: E(u) measures excess explained marginal-sign variance in convolution tensors, not temporal correlation. 19 trajectory entries plus14 meta-step entries contain32 unique runs (ml5/probe_w_m2_s0 repeats). Four clean peaks at1/1024 are lower-edge bounds. The clean meta-step amplitude ratio1.524 narrowly passes1.50 without the invalid1e-2 rung; the415× range includes that rung. Free coarse-granularity coordinate fields remain unmeasured.
original_question: Where in block size is the meta-gradient field's structure maximal, and is that location trajectory-invariant?

goal: Predict useful partitions from field measurements
comparison: Field-preferred scales and effective independence vs measured accuracy
why: Test whether a measurement can guide partition choice.
result: The scale bridge fails; later cc1 shows anti-concordance and dissociation.
reason: Better field readings do not consistently produce better accuracy.
scope: Historical K2 is20/21, with post-hoc resolved-only14/14; these must retain their original legacy-plateau provenance. The16/21 layerwise peaks and5.41-decade estimate are superseded by k=5 reanalysis: retain only≥2.71 decades/512× separation from the best region. Later registered cc1 (100ep,n=3,all12 box-free) directly rejects N_eff/m as a sufficient accuracy predictor.
original_question: THE BRIDGE — does 'the field has structure at scale X' imply 'partition at scale X' (the only way the measurement line becomes a method)?

goal: Explain the late-training correlation rebound
comparison: Original clipping vs box-free repeats and beta-velocity evidence
why: Test two proposed sources of the late rebound.
result: Rebound persists after unclipping; its cause remains unexplained.
reason: Both tested mechanisms fail; no third mechanism was registered.
scope: R10/C10 andR18/C100,20epochs,n=2. Rebound2.690→2.701 and2.577→2.583 while Q4 occupancy100%→0%. Scientifically unresolved, operationally closed by the historical CLOSEOUT9b decision; it is not a queued registered follow-up.
original_question: What causes the late-training (Q4) rebound in per-weight correlation?

goal: Verify the exponent contrast with independent estimators
comparison: Raw agreement, debiased agreement, and variance on matched runs
why: Test whether estimator bias drives the contrast.
